newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts hold gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts hold gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Friday in a fairly active session, with front months claiming modest gains after downside momentum stalled early in the day, industry sources said.
May gained 1.2 cents to close at $2.081 per million British thermal units. June settled 1.8 cents higher at $2.142. Others ended mixed, with some 1998s down slightly.

"I'd be a little careful here. We couldn't get over $2.095 (in May) two days in a row, and there's been a lot of new financial money in the market with only four days left to get out (before May expires Thursday)," said one Midwest trader.

While some traders did not rule out another run at key May resistance at $2.095, particularly if cash begins next week on a firm note, many remained cautious, noting the market was technically overbought and due for a correction.

In addition, fundamental traders were still concerned by prospects for milder spring weather soon and by current storage levels, particularly in the East where stocks are more than double last year's levels.
Chart traders said a May close above $2.095, the intraday high from March 10, should lead to a test of the $2.16 area. May support was seen at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825.
June, which hit another 11-week high of $2.145 today, seemed poised to test next resistance at the $2.21-2.23 gap from mid-January.

In the cash, Gulf Coast weekend prices firmed a couple of cents to about $2.05. Midcontinent pipes also were up slightly to the low-to-mid $1.90s. Weekend gas at the New York city gate fell a nickel to about the $2.40 level.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 0.6 cent to $2.241. NYMEX said 48,040 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 72,420.

On the KCBT, May finished 1.2 cents higher at $1.952, while deferreds ended steady to up by two cents. The East/West spread was unchanged at 12.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 244 lots changed hands, down from Thursday's total of 321.
